About Upstart
At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.
As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.
We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.
If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.
The Team
Upstart’s Partnerships team helps drive customer acquisition and originations through partner offers. The team is focused on improving how offers are optimized across the customer journey.
As the Applied Scientist on the Partnerships team, you’ll use causal inference, experimentation, and machine learning to help determine which offers are most likely to support customer conversion. You’ll take on a greenfield optimization opportunity, moving from research and measurement to production-ready models and decision strategies.
How you’ll make an impact
Develop causal machine-learning models to optimize customer offers at different points in the funnel, from marketing-time decisions with limited information to decisions informed by customer activity on our site.
Analyze and interpret complex data, identify gaps in what we know, and design experiments to gather evidence for building and evaluating optimization models.
Measure the impact of offer changes with statistically rigorous experiments and evaluations.
Translate research and results into clear recommendations, decision strategies, and next steps for business and technical partners.
Build production-ready models and code for use in offer selection.
Partner with Partnerships leadership, Product, Engineering, peer machine-learning teams, and model-risk partners to align on strategy, implementation, and methodology.
Minimum Qualifications
Graduate degree in mathematics, applied mathematics, statistics, physics, econometrics, operations research, computer science, or a related quantitative field.
2+ years of experience conducting machine-learning, statistical-modeling, or applied quantitative research in an academic or industry setting.
Experience applying causal inference methods and experimentation to real-world decisions in an applied-science or data-science context.
Applied statistics, probability, and experimental-design expertise used to build or evaluate models or interventions.
Production-quality coding experience in Python, including data manipulation and algorithm implementation.
Preferred Qualifications
PhD in a quantitative field.
Experience with marketplace optimization, particularly where pricing or offer decisions are central.
Experience with causal machine-learning methods or treatment-effect modeling.
Experience with supervised learning, model evaluation, and feature engineering, especially with large or complex datasets.
Experience taking work from exploratory analysis and experimentation through production-model development while maintaining analytical rigor and model reliability.
Ability to translate broad business problems into structured research questions and communicate complex findings as actionable recommendations.

About the company
General Matter enriches uranium.
We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.
In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.
Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume.  Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.
Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable.  We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.
We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.
Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.
We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.
Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.
About This Role
We're looking for a New Graduate Engineer with a strong interest in regulatory compliance and licensing to join our growing engineering team. You'll collaborate with experienced engineers to support licensing actions, regulatory submissions, and engagement with regulatory authorities for a nuclear fuel cycle facility. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated graduate eager to contribute to high-reliability, highly regulated nuclear facility work.
Responsibilities
Support the preparation and review of licensing documents, including licensing applications, regulatory reports, amendment requests, and license renewal applications, in compliance with NRC requirements.
Assist in communication with regulatory agencies such as the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and help track timely resolution of inquiries.
Support the development and implementation of strategies to obtain and maintain licenses for new and existing nuclear facilities and projects.
Perform technical evaluations under the guidance of senior engineers to help ensure compliance with applicable codes, standards, and regulations (e.g., 10 CFR).
Help monitor changes to nuclear regulations and assess their impact on operations and licensing.
Support safety analyses, environmental reports, and risk assessments to ensure regulatory compliance.
Work on documentation and technical writing to support licensing submissions and regulatory correspondence.
Collaborate with engineering, operations, legal, and environmental teams to help address licensing requirements and resolve regulatory issues.
Participate in inspections, audits, and regulatory meetings alongside senior team members.
Effectively communicate technical ideas within multidisciplinary project teams.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Nuclear Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field (recent graduate or upcoming).
Coursework in nuclear engineering fundamentals, reactor physics, or fuel cycle systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear and concise technical documentation.
Strong organizational and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Ability to communicate technical information clearly and collaboratively across disciplines.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Internship experience in nuclear licensing, regulatory affairs, or a related technical role, especially projects involving nuclear or highly regulated facilities
General familiarity with NRC regulations, including 10 CFR and related industry standards (e.g., ANSI, ASME).
Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc.).
Familiarity with nuclear facility operations and safety analyses.
Exposure to interacting with regulatory agencies, such as the NRC.
Additional Requirements
Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.
